memo.verdict: Park. Neutral on the shares at 941.0 PLN (2026-10-06); bullish on the business. Two triggers to progress: a price at or below about 800 PLN, where the modal path clears 20% a year over three years and the multiple risk shrinks toward the five-year median; or the Q3 2026 results on 12 November 2026 showing a gross margin at or above 30% without currency help and Stęszew on budget, which would move the modal multiple toward 10x and the return toward 16 to 18% a year. The park rule is not tripped: management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability A. Conviction medium at Triaging depth; the least secure judgement is the modal multiple of 9.5x, and the fact that would most change it is the Q3 2026 gross margin. The record names no invalidate condition for the case itself beyond the measured series: a quarterly gross margin below 28.5% without a currency explanation; inventory days above 140; EUR/PLN above 4.40 for a quarter with the gross margin falling; consolidated monthly sales growth below 8%.
case: A cleared-concern case in a scale compounder, bought after the clearing has been priced. The company grows 12 to 15% against a European distribution market growing about 2.0% a year ex-inflation (CEE 4 to 6%) by taking share from a faltering largest rival (LKQ Europe organic −4.8% in Q4 2025, −5.1% in Q2 2026, −12.6% in Germany) and from sub-scale players, with the foreign subsidiaries as the engine (28 new foreign branches in twelve months; first German B2B branch May 2026; ambition of 300 to 400 German locations). Earnings were flat from FY2021 to FY2025 because parts prices deflated (−3.7% in 2025), the zloty strengthened, and the company stocked two automated hubs (Zakroczym PLN 235m with 555 robots; Brașov about PLN 222m with 250-plus; 900 fewer warehouse staff; first-phase savings about PLN 25m a year), so free cash flow on the standardised definition was negative every year (FY2025 PLN −88.7m) and the EBITDA margin fell from 8.3% in FY2021 to 6.3% in FY2024.

In 2026 all three turned. Parts prices rose 1.5% quarter on quarter in Q2 2026 (premium segments +2.6%); the gross margin stepped to 30.1% in H1 2026 from 29.0%, of which 0.1 to 0.2 percentage points is currency and the rest purchasing scale and inflation pass-through on 134 days of stock, and Auto Partner's gross margin moved the same way (29.3% in Q2 2026 from 25.4% in Q1 2025), which says it is the market and not one company's timing; SG&A is 14.4% of sales against LKQ's 28.7%; net working capital fell to 27.5% of revenue at Q2 2026 from 32.4% at Q3 2025. The change has reached every layer of the chain: a stable team; organic-and-automation choices; branches and hubs as actions; gross margin and SG&A as key metrics; the H1 2026 statements; the sell-side's estimates (FY2026 consensus EPS +10.2% over three months and +10.1% over six; FY2027 +8.8% and +13.9%; FY2028 +12.1% over three months; Noble EBITDA +17/19/19% for 2026 to 2028; no visible cut). It is a mature change.

The record's modal path: revenue +12.5%, +10.5%, +9.0% for FY2026 to FY2028 (PLN 23,868m to PLN 28,748m); EBITDA PLN 1,817m in FY2026 (+27.6%) rising to PLN 2,357m in FY2028; EBITDA margin 7.6%, 7.9%, 8.2%, a recovery to the FY2021 to FY2022 level of 8.1 to 8.3% plus the first contribution from Stęszew, most of the claimed point held back until the hub runs; EPS 75.0 PLN (+31%, about 1.3 PLN of it the insurance one-off), 87.6 PLN (+16.8%), 102.1 PLN (+16.5%), 116.0 PLN (+13.6%). The decomposition reconciles: revenue ×1.107, margin ×1.069 (EBITDA 18.3% a year), below-EBITDA ×1.024 (conversion 56.6% to 60.8%; depreciation PLN 306m, PLN 352m, PLN 382m; net interest PLN 189m in FY2025 and PLN 98m in H1 2026, falling on the bank-margin grid; tax 19.8%; no minorities), shares ×1.000 (14.02m, incentive issuance of up to 400,000 shares offsetting the 2025 buyback of 150,000 at 575.00 PLN), product 21.2% a year against the claim of 21.4%; from FY2026 to FY2029 the rate is 15.6% a year, the figure to carry. Modal EPS growth sits inside the 12 to 20% band from FY2027 and above it in FY2026 (over-extrapolation risk marked).
counter_case: At its strongest: Inter Cars is the risk research's false friend, and the market has just paid a five-year-high multiple for it. The H1 2026 margin was lifted by a stronger zloty on euro-denominated purchases, by a PLN 23m insurance gain the company did not call out while telling the call the margin gain was entirely structural, and by a one-quarter turn in parts prices that a three-year Polish price war can reverse the moment inflation cools, which management itself warns could happen in late 2026. Underneath, the business converts earnings to cash poorly (free cash flow negative on the standardised definition in every year FY2021 to FY2025; free cash flow to net income −15%, −55%, −7%, −40%, −11%), holds about PLN 6.0bn of inventory at 134 days with 0.58% provisioning against peers' 2 to 4%, runs an estimated 60% of cost of goods in euros against 24% of revenue with no hedge at all (zero forwards, options or swaps in 2023 to 2025; no interest-rate derivatives), capitalises interest on automation loans and the Warsaw takeover fee, guarantees PLN 1,054.7m of related-party debt at the parent with PLN 400.6m of related-party loans, and relies for its exports on a 25% Polish price gap that suppliers intend to close by about 2030, with the parent's direct exports already down 10%. Its largest foreign market, Romania, is in recession (GDP −2.0% in Q2 2026, an 8.2% current-account deficit, a collapsed coalition); its employee net promoter score halved to 10% in 2025 with 25% turnover in 2024; its largest franchise partner in the capital walked; its revenue targets were missed three years running (18% against 20% in 2023; 8% against 13 to 15% in 2024; 97.6% of target in 2025) and Q4 2023 net profit was PLN 119m against PLN 188m of consensus; internal control is dispersed by the company's own admission; Auto Partner delivers more often (thirty to forty-five customers a route against twenty), matched the gross margin at 29.3%, and is building a 24,300 square-metre German hub. On this reading the FY2026 earnings jump of 31% is a cyclical margin recovery sold as structural, consensus is extrapolating it (FY2028 EPS +15.8%), the gross margin fell from 29.5% in FY2021 to 28.1% in FY2023 when the zloty strengthened and deflation set in so it has been cyclical before, and a stock at the 84th percentile of its range on a 5% EBIT margin with 20 to 30% of multiple downside is a short-side setup, not a long. The downside case is coherent and priced: fair value 648 PLN on a 29.9% gross margin, a 7.0% EBITDA margin and 6.5x EV/EBITDA, 31% below the price; the five-year median multiple of 7.85x gives about 747 PLN and the ten-year crash band about 695 PLN with earnings unchanged. The multiple is company-driven, so nothing in a de-rating sector (peers at the 0th to 50th percentiles of their own ranges; six of seven at D or F on sell-side momentum) holds it up, and Erste's technician has already called a channel break with a path to 600 PLN. The combination that would bite is a zloty fall during a Polish price war while Stęszew is being stocked, on a Pret sandwich of individually tolerable weaknesses.

The record concedes every fact in it: the cash record is poor; the hedging policy is a bet; the one-off was not disclosed cleanly; the export arbitrage is eroding; the multiple is at the top of its five-year range; the H1 margin had 0.2 percentage points of currency help and 0.4 of one-off in Q2. The record holds its view on the business because the gross-margin decomposition says only 0.1 to 0.2 points of the 1.1-point gain is currency and the peer moved with it; the working-capital build is the inventory for two new hubs and is already turning (net working capital 27.5% of revenue from 32.4%; operating cash flow PLN 792.7m in H1 2026); consensus free cash flow turns positive in FY2026 and reaches PLN 842m by FY2028; the export arbitrage is a parent business being replaced by subsidiaries on purpose; the guarantees are to the group's own logistics entities, audited without qualification; and growth of 12% in euro terms against a sector median of about 4% is share gain by a better-run network, not a currency effect. The record does not hold its view on the price: the counter-case is why the modal multiple is 9.5x rather than 10.6x, why the return is a C, and why the recommendation is to wait for 800 PLN or the Q3 print. A second counter-case, at Building Block 4, argues the opposite direction: that four pinned Bs and the ten-year lens (26th percentile; room to the prudent median of 10.6x, which gives 22.0% a year over eighteen months) make the case a B; the record concedes the arithmetic and holds C because the ten-year multiples were earned at 20%-plus EPS growth with positive free cash flow, growth decelerates to 13 to 15% beyond FY2028, and the peers' multiples are falling, so the re-rating branch is possible, not probable, and a case that needs it is not crisp.
triggers: - Which valuation window is right, the five-year (re-rating done, 84th percentile) or the ten-year (26th percentile, room to 10.6x): the open question of the case; the Q3 2026 gross margin is the fact that settles it.
- Progress trigger 1: price at or below about 800 PLN (the modal path clears 20% a year over three years from about 780 PLN and over eighteen months from 865 PLN).

- Progress trigger 2: Q3 2026 results on 12 November 2026 with the gross margin at or above 30% without currency help and Stęszew on budget; this would move the modal multiple toward 10x and the return toward 16 to 18%. Also what would change the re-rating odds: consensus FY2028 EPS above 105 PLN.
- Gross margin: alarm a quarter below 29.5%; invalidate a quarter below 28.5% without a currency explanation (the earnings review's own level); the 'Foundations' would be C at that level.
- Parts-price index (Noble): confirm positive quarter on quarter; alarm a flat or negative quarter.
- Stęszew: alarm capex above PLN 215m in a half-year without a launch date; watch the launch about the end of the first quarter of 2027 and the first-year saving against Zakroczym's PLN 25m a year.
